title: History Has No Chill
blurb: Revolutions, empires, inventors and true stories too weird to make up. Except one.

cards.say: [Revolutionary France briefly used clocks with 10 hours in a day], [the Bastille held more than 100 prisoners on the day it was stormed], [the metric system was born during the French Revolution], and [Haiti became a nation after a successful revolt by enslaved people].
cards.real: When crowds stormed the Bastille on July 14, 1789, it held just seven prisoners.

cards.say: [Mark Twain patented a scrapbook with the glue already on its pages], [a 15-year-old in Maine came up with an improved design for earmuffs], [a woman fed up with her chipped china patented a dishwasher in 1886], and [a 12-year-old girl invented a machine to make flat-bottomed paper bags].
cards.real: Margaret Knight was about 30 when she invented her paper bag machine in 1868. At 12, she'd come up with a safety device for mill looms.

cards.say: [Marie Curie won Nobel Prizes in both physics and medicine], [Isaac Newton worked at England's Royal Mint hunting down counterfeiters], [Albert Einstein was once offered the job of president of Israel], and [Ada Lovelace, often called the first programmer, was Lord Byron's daughter].
cards.real: Marie Curie won the 1903 Nobel Prize in Physics and the 1911 Nobel Prize in Chemistry. She never won one for medicine.

cards.say: [Sweden once had a February 30, in the year 1712], [Russia's October Revolution happened in November on our calendar], [Britain skipped an entire month in 1752 to fix its calendar], and [Julius Caesar made the year 46 BC last 445 days].
cards.real: Britain skipped 11 days, not a month: in 1752, September 2 was followed straight by September 14.
src: NOT WEB-CHECKED (textbook) Caesar's calendar reform stretched 46 BC to 445 days so the new Julian calendar could start in step with the seasons https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/46_BC

cards.say: [a European world map from 1375 shows Mali's king Mansa Musa], [Alexander the Great named a city after his horse], [Rome built Hadrian's Wall to keep out Viking raiders], and [the Inca kept their empire's records on knotted strings].
cards.real: Hadrian's Wall went up around AD 122, more than 650 years before the first Viking raids on Britain. It guarded Rome's border against northern tribes.
src: NOT WEB-CHECKED (textbook) Hadrian's Wall was begun in AD 122; the first recorded Viking raids on Britain came in the 790s https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hadrian%27s_Wall

cards.say: [Paul Revere made his famous midnight ride all by himself], [most signers of the Declaration of Independence signed it in August], [the Battle of New Orleans was fought after the peace treaty was signed], and [Mozart wrote music for an instrument invented by Benjamin Franklin].
cards.real: Revere didn't ride alone: William Dawes took another route, and Samuel Prescott joined them. Only Prescott made it all the way to Concord.

cards.say: [the first person to survive going over Niagara Falls in a barrel was a 63-year-old teacher], [a dancing plague in 1518 left people in Strasbourg dancing for days], [Bertha Benz took the first long car trip without telling her husband], and [the world's first speeding ticket went to Henry Ford in Detroit].
cards.real: The first speeding conviction went to Walter Arnold in Kent, England, in 1896, for going 8 mph in a 2 mph zone.

cards.say: [Peter the Great put a tax on beards in Russia], [Catherine the Great was born and raised in Russia], [Lady Jane Grey was deposed nine days after being proclaimed queen], and [Louis XIV became king of France at age four].
cards.real: Catherine the Great was a German princess, born in Stettin in Prussia. She moved to Russia as a teenager to marry the future tsar.

cards.say: [Super Glue was discovered in World War II and rejected for being too sticky], [the Frisbee got its name from a pie company in Connecticut], [Alexander Graham Bell wanted phone calls to start with the word ahoy], and [Velcro was invented by an engineer who studied how gecko feet stick].
cards.real: Velcro came from burrs. George de Mestral got the idea in 1941 after pulling prickly burrs off his clothes and his dog.

cards.say: [Pablo Picasso was questioned by police after the Mona Lisa was stolen in 1911], [Michelangelo painted the Sistine Chapel ceiling in 10 months], [Salvador Dalí designed the logo for Chupa Chups lollipops], and [Shakespeare's Globe Theatre burned down after a stage cannon set its roof on fire in 1613].
cards.real: Michelangelo spent about four years on the Sistine Chapel ceiling, from 1508 to 1512.

cards.say: [Margaret Thatcher was the first woman ever elected prime minister], [New Zealand let women vote in national elections in 1893], [Monopoly is based on a game a woman made to show how landlords get rich], and [windshield wipers were patented by a woman, Mary Anderson, in 1903].
cards.real: Sri Lanka's Sirimavo Bandaranaike became the world's first female prime minister in 1960, almost 20 years before Thatcher.

cards.say: [ancient Egyptian tomb builders went on strike when their supplies ran late], [an ancient Greek gadget found in a shipwreck could predict eclipses], [the Great Pyramid of Giza was built as a tomb for King Tut], and [Great Zimbabwe's huge stone walls were built without any mortar].
cards.real: The Great Pyramid was built for the pharaoh Khufu around 2600 BC, more than a thousand years before Tutankhamun was born.
